saved % = (original KB − new KB) ÷ original KB × 100
target met when new size ≤ target size
howTo: Click “Choose PDF file” and select the PDF you want to shrink.
Pick a mode: Recommended for everyday use, Strong for maximum shrink, or Target size for a strict limit like 200 KB.
If you chose Target size, enter the size in KB (200 is the common form-upload preset).
Click “Compress PDF” and wait for the passes to finish.
Compare the before/after sizes, then download the compressed PDF.
keyFacts: Most PDF size comes from embedded photos: a single full-page JPEG can weigh several megabytes.
This tool finds JPEG images inside the PDF, downscales them and re-encodes them at a lower quality — the same technique desktop tools use.
The PDF structure is rebuilt with object streams (useObjectStreams), which packs the file's internal objects more tightly.
Target-size mode runs up to six passes with shrinking dimensions (1920 → 640 px) and quality (75% → 28%) until the target is met.
Only JPEG (DCTDecode) images are recompressed; PNG and other image types are left untouched.

compress-pdf.workedExample:
An 8.4 MB scanned report (8,400 KB) compressed in Recommended mode comes out at 2.1 MB (2,100 KB):
saved % = (8,400 − 2,100) ÷ 8,400 × 100 = 75%
Three quarters of the file size was photo data that the downscaling removed.
